changes.before: the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/2 to 3/4 percent
changes.after: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3/4 to 1 percent

changes.before: Inflation increased in recent quarters but is still below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective.
changes.after: Inflation has increased in recent quarters, moving close to the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective; excluding energy and food prices, inflation was little changed and continued to run somewhat below 2 percent.

changes.before: inflation will rise to 2 percent over the medium term
changes.after: inflation will stabilize around 2 percent over the medium term

changes.before: In light of the current shortfall of inflation from 2 percent, the Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected progress toward its inflation goal.
changes.after: The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal.

changes.before: will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate
changes.after: will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate

changes.before: business fixed investment has remained soft
changes.after: business fixed investment appears to have firmed somewhat

changes.before: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Janet L. Yellen, Chair; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Lael Brainard; Charles L. Evans; Stanley Fischer; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Jerome H. Powell; and Daniel K. Tarullo.
changes.after: Voting against the action was Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.

parsed.rationale: The Committee raised rates and upgraded its inflation and investment assessments, though it kept the gradual-path guidance and added 'symmetric' goal language that tempers the hawkishness. A dovish dissent further softens the signal, so the shift is moderately hawkish rather than a regime change.

Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Janet L. Yellen, Chair; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Lael Brainard; Charles L. Evans; Stanley Fischer; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Jerome H. Powell; and Daniel K. Tarullo.

inflation will stabilize around 2 percent over the medium term
The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal.
will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate

Voting against the action was Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.
